Footer.heading: Independent publication
Footer.body: Compiled from publicly available sources. This is not an official publication and has no affiliation with any manufacturer or government body. Brand names are used for identification purposes only.

Home.heading: One field, {sources} sources, {values} different values.
Home.headingPlain: Every value carries the source that published it.
Home.lead: Açık Dosya keeps technical files on Turkish defence industry systems. Next to every figure it puts the source that published it, the date it was verified and a confidence level.
Home.leadSecondary: Conflicting values are not filtered out. All of them stay in the file, and you decide which one to use.
Home.filesCount: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} published
Home.methodIntro: Every value carries one of three states. The state does not say the value is correct; it describes the quality of its source. The same three states look identical in the table, the map legend, the 3D labels and the timeline.
Home.conflictBody: When several sources publish a value, all of them are listed. But more than one value does not mean a contradiction: “> 280 km” and “> 500 km” are both lower bounds, and both can be true at once. Which case applies is computed from the operators, not flagged by hand.
Home.headingRevision: Every figure that changed says why.

SystemPage.datasetDescription: Measurement record compiled from public sources. Every figure carries its confidence level and source; conflicting figures are kept, not resolved.

RangeEnvelope.intro: Drag the reference point to move it. The rings are geodesic projections of published range figures; they do not show a flight profile or operational use.
RangeEnvelope.mapLabel: Range envelope map, reference point is draggable
RangeEnvelope.legend: Rings are drawn along great circles — a flat circle on a Mercator projection introduces serious error at high latitudes. The figures come from public statements and contradict each other: a dashed ring is press-sourced, a red ring is an estimate with no official confirmation.

ModelViewer.note: The schematic look is deliberate: a photorealistic render would claim an accuracy we do not have. There is no cross-section, exploded view or internal component layout — we hold no sourced data on internal geometry. Labels name external sections only and each carries its own confidence level. The body is derived from published length and diameter values; it is not a technical drawing.

ConfidenceLevels.official: The manufacturer's or the institution's own statement. A link is given; if the link dies, an archive copy replaces it and the date is recorded. The official badge shows who the statement came from; it does not show that the information has been independently verified.
ConfidenceLevels.press: Secondary source: news report, magazine, trade show or conference note. Unverified, but on record and not hidden.
ConfidenceLevels.estimate: Independent assessment with no official confirmation. Its badge is red, because this is an inference rather than a statement.

Method.title: Source, confidence and conflict
Method.lead: This page explains how the files are built: when a figure gets published, what the confidence level says, and why conflicting values are not hidden.
Method.levelsIntro: Every value carries one of three states. The state does not say the value is correct; it describes the quality of its source.
Method.levelsNote: The three states differ by pattern as well as colour: solid border, dashed border, red border with a soft fill. They stay readable in colour blindness and in black and white print. The same three states look identical in the table, the map legend, the 3D labels and the timeline.
Method.recordIntro: A figure without a confidence level never reaches the interface. There is no exception: the field stays empty rather than being filled with an invented value.
Method.termBody_value: The figure itself and its operator, if any. "> 280" is not the same value as "280"; when the source gives a bound, the bound is recorded.
Method.termBody_confidence: Official, press or estimate. It describes the quality of the source.
Method.termBody_source: The human-readable name of the body or publication that released the value, with a link where one exists.
Method.termBody_verified: When the record was last checked. Six months from now, this field answers the question of where a figure came from.
Method.recordUnits: The unit lives inside the field name rather than in a field of its own. Confusing metres with millimetres is therefore impossible.
Method.recordMissing: Where there is no data, a dash is shown and screen readers hear "no data". Missing data is not a fourth confidence state; it says the record is empty there.
Method.conflictHeading: Why we do not hide conflicts
Method.conflictIntro: Open-source figures diverge from each other. Picking one and deleting the rest means making an editorial decision the reader cannot see. Instead they all sit stacked in the same cell, each carrying its own source.
Method.conflictPick: Where only one figure fits, such as the scaled silhouette and the 3D model, the most reliable value is used: official, then press, then estimate. That choice affects the drawing, not the record — the table keeps showing all of them.
Method.divergenceIntro: More than one value in the same field is not a contradiction on its own. Which case applies is computed from the operators and the scope fields, not flagged by hand. There are three outcomes.
Method.divergence_celiski: The intervals do not overlap: no number can satisfy both. Either one source is wrong, or the two are in fact talking about different things. This is rare, which is why the row is marked.
Method.divergence_farkliAciklama: The intervals overlap, so both can be true at once. Lower bounds work this way: “> 280” and “> 500” do not contradict each other, the second already satisfies the first. This is a normal state, not a warning.
Method.divergence_farkliKapsam: The values are not measuring the same thing: they were obtained by different methods, belong to different variants, or were stated on different dates. No interval arithmetic is done here, because the values are not comparable. Which field differs is written under the value.
Method.divergenceExampleIntro: The three rows below are HYPOTHETICAL. They belong to no system and are not taken from the files; they only show how the calculation works.
Method.divergenceExample_celiski: “< 6 m” and “> 9 m” — contradiction. No length is both under 6 and over 9.
Method.divergenceExample_farkliAciklama: “> 6 m” and “> 9 m” — different statements. Any body longer than 9 metres satisfies both.
Method.divergenceExample_farkliKapsam: “9 m” (third-party measurement) and “> 6 m” (declared) — different scope. One measured the object, the other stated a figure.
Method.divergenceScope: Scope is carried in three fields: how the value was obtained (declared, measured in a test, third-party measurement, inference), which variant it belongs to, and the date the statement was made. When these are unknown they are left empty and the value reads “scope not stated”. They are never filled in by guesswork.
Method.divergenceBadgeNote: The official badge shows who the statement came from; it does not show that the information has been independently verified. A figure being official does not mean we measured it, or that anyone else confirmed it.
Method.limitsIntro: Some material is findable in open sources and still stays out of these files. The limit is editorial rather than technical.
Method.limit_targets: No target language. A range ring is drawn; no target city or country is labelled or highlighted. The terms used are "range envelope" and "reference point".
Method.limit_classes: No list of the target classes a system was developed against.
Method.limit_internals: No technical detail on production, guidance internals, warhead design or accuracy optimisation. The limit is this: dimensions, mass, programme timeline and published performance claims.
Method.correctionsBody: If you believe a value is wrong, or you hold a better source, send it. Every sourced correction goes on record. Contact details are <link>on the about page</link>.

About.title: Açık Dosya
About.lead: An independent publication keeping sourced technical files on Turkish defence industry systems.
About.independenceBody: Açık Dosya is an independent publication. It has no affiliation with any institution, manufacturer or government body, receives no support from any of them and represents none of them. These pages are not an official publication.
About.independenceBrands: Brand, system and institution names are used for identification only and belong to their owners. Manufacturer logos are not used.
About.scopeBody: We cover a small number of systems in depth. This is not a catalogue or an encyclopaedia: each file holds sourced data, a scaled drawing, a programme timeline and a range envelope. There is no news feed and no user-contributed content.
About.scopeMethod: How a figure enters the record is described <link>on the method page</link>.
About.privacyBody: Visits are counted by a meter running on our own server. No cookies are used and none are sent with requests, so there is no consent banner. If your browser says it does not want to be tracked (Do Not Track), nothing is recorded.
About.privacyRequests: The page makes no request to a third-party server: fonts, the map base layer and the analytics file are all served from this address. Query strings are not recorded — the reference point you choose on the range envelope never reaches us.
About.contactBody: Write for corrections, missing sources and questions.
About.contactWhat: When sending a correction, say which system, which field and which source you mean. Reports without a source cannot enter the record.
